create_client_token.description: Generate a client token used to initialize Braintree's client-side SDKs (Drop-in UI, Hosted Fields, or the mobile SDKs).
create_client_token.name: create_client_token

parameters.description: Scope the token to a specific merchant account, for example a non-default currency (optional).
parameters.name: merchant_account_id

returns.description: Object with a 'clientToken' string to hand to a Braintree client SDK.

create_transaction.description: Charge a payment method (a client-generated nonce or a vaulted token) for a given amount.
create_transaction.name: create_transaction

parameters.description: A single-use payment method nonce or a vaulted payment method token to charge. In the sandbox you can use 'fake-valid-nonce' to simulate a successful card.
parameters.name: payment_method_id

parameters.description: The amount to charge as a decimal string, for example '10.00'. Use the account's default currency.
parameters.name: amount

parameters.description: Your own order or invoice reference (optional).
parameters.name: order_id

returns.description: Braintree transaction object with its id, status, amount, and order id.

get_transaction.description: Look up one transaction: its status, amount, order ID and customer.
get_transaction.name: get_transaction

parameters.description: The transaction's ID, from Search transactions or the New transaction trigger, or the short ID the Control Panel shows.
parameters.name: transaction_id

customer_first_name.description: The customer's first name, if known

customer_id.description: The vaulted customer it belongs to, if any

customer_last_name.description: The customer's last name, if known

id.description: The transaction's ID, for the refund and reverse steps

legacy_id.description: The short ID the Control Panel shows

merchant_account_id.description: The merchant account it was made in

order_id.description: Your own order or invoice reference, if one was given

status.description: Its status, such as SUBMITTED_FOR_SETTLEMENT, SETTLED, VOIDED or PROCESSOR_DECLINED

refund_transaction.description: Refund a settled transaction, in full or in part. Use Reverse a transaction instead if it has not settled yet.
refund_transaction.name: refund_transaction

parameters.description: The ID of the settled transaction to refund.
parameters.name: transaction_id

parameters.description: The amount to refund as a decimal string, for example '5.00'. Leave blank to refund the full amount.
parameters.name: amount

returns.description: Braintree refund object with its id, status, and amount.

reverse_transaction.description: Cancel a transaction. Braintree voids it if it has not settled yet, or refunds it in full if it already has.
reverse_transaction.name: reverse_transaction

parameters.description: The ID of the transaction to reverse.
parameters.name: transaction_id

returns.description: Braintree reversal object: either the voided transaction or a refund, distinguished by its __typename.

search_transactions.description: Search recent transactions, optionally filtered by status.
search_transactions.name: search_transactions

parameters.description: Filter by transaction status, for example 'SETTLED', 'SUBMITTED_FOR_SETTLEMENT', 'VOIDED', or 'PROCESSOR_DECLINED'. Leave blank to return the most recent transactions of any status.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Maximum transactions to return (Braintree caps a page at 50).
parameters.name: first

items.description: Braintree transaction with its id, status, amount, and order id.

description: Accept card and digital-wallet payments and automate refunds with Braintree, a PayPal service.

braintree_new_transaction_trigger.description: Runs for each new transaction in your Braintree account, whether it went through or was declined, with its status, amount, order ID and customer. Transactions already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.customer_first_name: The customer's first name, if known.
output.customer_id: The vaulted customer it belongs to, if any.
output.customer_last_name: The customer's last name, if known.
output.id: The transaction's ID, for Get, Refund or Reverse a transaction.
output.legacy_id: The short ID the Control Panel shows.
output.merchant_account_id: The merchant account it was made in.
output.order_id: Your own order or invoice reference, if one was given.
output.status: Its status when it was found, such as SUBMITTED_FOR_SETTLEMENT, AUTHORIZED, PROCESSOR_DECLINED or GATEWAY_REJECTED.
